rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.2, field experiments 2012-2014 at Shihezi, Xinjiang, with five fertilizer levels x three drip irrigation levels in a replicated factorial design; Tables 3-4 and Figs 2-3 report own measurements of LAI, boll weight, dry matter, seed cotton yield, WUE, PFP and economic benefits.
rows.notes: All treatments are under mulched drip fertigation; the experiment varies irrigation amount (0.6/0.8/1.0 ETc) and N-P2O5-K2O rate, with no comparison of drip against another irrigation method. The results are therefore evidence about water and fertilizer rates under drip, not about drip irrigation improving yield, quality or water/fertilizer productivity. The study shows yield, dry matter and economic benefits increase with irrigation amount up to 1.0 ETc and peak at 300-120-60 kg/ha fertilizer in 2012 and 2014; WUE is highest under deficit irrigation and PFP declines with fertilizer rate; multi-objective regression gives optimal ranges of 362-463 mm water and 212-368 kg/ha N. Fiber quality was not measured. Bars show standard errors (n=3) for yield-related variables, but these pertain to the water x fertilizer effect, not to drip per se.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.2 and Tables 1, 3, 4; three-year replicated field experiment on drip-fertigated cotton with measured irrigation amounts, yield, WUE and economic benefits.
rows.notes: The study does not evaluate drip irrigation as a water-saving technology relative to any alternative; it compares deficit (0.6, 0.8 ETc) with full (1.0 ETc) drip irrigation. It finds that reducing irrigation raised WUE but caused large yield and economic losses, and that water fees are a small share of costs so farmers' willingness to save water is weak. These are results about irrigation amount under drip, not about drip saving water. No water-saving effect of drip itself is reported.

notes: Full text appears complete. Single-site (sandy loam, Shihezi), single-cultivar-per-year field experiment, 2012-2014, all plots under plastic-mulched drip fertigation; no non-drip control, so the study cannot provide own evidence on drip irrigation effects per se for either claim.
